heading: Last-mile questions, answered.
description: Everything you need to know before trying Helix — from how orchestration works to how we handle pricing and security.

items.question: What exactly is Helix?
items.answer: Helix is an atomic work-breakdown orchestrator for AI coding agents. Instead of asking an agent to ship a sprawling diff in one shot, Helix decomposes every prompt into small, reviewable units, executes them in order with explicit dependencies, verifies each unit against your repo (types, tests, lint), and emits small, reviewable PRs.

items.question: How does the orchestration actually work?
items.answer: You describe the goal. Helix decomposes it into atoms — atomic units of work — with explicit dependency edges. Each atom runs against your repo, is verified locally (types, tests, lint), and is opened as a single, focused PR. Atoms with no dependencies run in parallel; downstream atoms wait for their upstream PRs to merge.

items.question: Which integrations are supported?
items.answer: Helix ships with GitHub for source control and PR creation, works with any agent that emits structured diffs, and integrates with the standard CI toolchain (GitHub Actions, Vercel builds, arbitrary runners). The orchestrator itself is open-source, so additional integrations are first-class PRs back into the project.

items.question: How do I deploy Helix?
items.answer: Clone the repo, set the GITHUB_TOKEN and a model API key, and run npm run dev for local use or push to Vercel for a hosted deploy. The provided vercel.json configures the build, install, and dev commands and sets sane security headers out of the box.

items.question: Is there a pricing tier?
items.answer: Helix itself is open-source under the repository's license. You only pay for the compute and model API calls you actually consume — the orchestrator is free. Future hosted tiers will be optional and additive, never required to run Helix locally.

items.question: How does Helix handle secrets and security?
items.answer: All secrets stay local to your runner — Helix never proxies your tokens or diffs through a third-party service. The orchestrator runs inside your CI, against your repo, with your permissions. Security headers (nosniff, DENY framing, strict referrer policy, locked-down permissions policy) ship by default for the marketing site and can be tuned in vercel.json.

items.question: Can Helix damage my repository?
items.answer: No. Every atomic unit opens as a draft PR — nothing merges automatically. You review and merge each PR on your terms. If an atom fails verification, the orchestrator stops the chain and surfaces the failure, so a broken intermediate never reaches your main branch.

items.question: Can I contribute?
items.answer: Yes. Helix is open-source. Open a PR against the canonical repo, follow the contributing guidelines in the README, and tag the relevant maintainer. Small, well-scoped PRs are reviewed fastest — which is, fittingly, the same philosophy Helix brings to AI-generated code.
